wcs_p1_first_half: Say you've been at something for weeks and not much is changing. It's tempting to call the whole method a dud, or else to keep doing the exact same thing forever so you never have to admit it isn't working. Did you actually get to the part you meant to practice, or did you mostly read about it and get ready to? Reading this article counts as getting ready, sorry. 😅
wcs_p1_second_half: And was the grown-up you needed really there? If you're trying to comfort your little one and the loving grown-up just isn't there yet, more loving sentences won't fix that. It's like getting hugged by someone who's checking their phone. I'd borrow that grown-up first, then come back to your little one.
wcs_p2a_littleone: Some things should shift pretty fast, and some are more like learning guitar, so I wouldn't pick a magic number of tries. If it's making things worse, though, I'd change course sooner, since your little one is the one who has to sit through it. Same if it just isn't doable right now. Not wanting to do it anymore can count too, but I'd hear that no out first, sudden or not, since it might be a part of you that's trying to protect you. And if what the method said would happen keeps not happening, even when you're doing it right, or something clearly better supported comes along, that's a reason to switch.
